claims.text: The proposed feedstock is a Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti powder mixture containing a hydride precursor such as TiH2.
Interstitial oxygen introduced during preparation of NbMoTaWVTi can produce an unintended TiO precipitate.
Processing the hydride-containing powder requires a two-stage thermal history consisting of low-temperature decomposition followed by hot extrusion.
Hydride decomposition should be conducted at 300-400°C for two hours.
Decomposition below 400°C removes hydrogen without triggering oxidation of Ti.
The decomposition atmosphere must be ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa or an inert atmosphere containing less than 1 ppm O2 and N2.
Hot extrusion should be performed at 1100-1200°C and a strain rate below 0.1 s^-1.
A low strain rate or higher processing temperature may permit hot deformation of an oxygen-containing refractory high-entropy alloy.
Low-strain-rate hot extrusion promotes dynamic recovery and dynamic recrystallization.
Maintaining low oxygen activity during processing suppresses TiO nucleation in NbMoTaWVTi.
Rapid hydrogen removal and high-temperature deformation inhibit alpha-HCP transformation by thermodynamically stabilizing the BCC solid solution.
Grain-boundary-localized oxides and Laves phases promote crack initiation and low plasticity.
The proposed thermal and deformation schedule avoids the brittle temperature regime and prevents catastrophic cracking.
The process will produce a dense, crack-free bulk alloy.
The processed bulk alloy will retain a single-phase BCC structure.
The process will reduce oxygen content below 100 ppm.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength above 600 MPa at 700°C.
Eliminating brittle precipitates enhances high-temperature yield strength.
Mechanical alloying can introduce high oxygen levels that promote brittleness and oxide formation.
The exact hydride-decomposition window that avoids concurrent oxidation in NbMoTaWVTi has not been experimentally quantified in the cited records.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa is required, whereas the conditions allow either ultra-high vacuum or an inert gas with less than 1 ppm O2/N2. These are materially different environmental requirements.

The predicted oxygen target is below 100 ppm, but oxygen does not falsify the hypothesis until it exceeds 0.5 wt% (about 5000 ppm). Thus a result far above the predicted target could still avoid the stated falsification criterion.
